# Open choices: apis-and-services

`aidd-team:apis-and-services` leaves these decisions to the team. aidd's default holds until a `standards` entry fills one. `aidd standard list` names the library standards for each choice, and `aidd standard add` adopts one.

| Choice | Question | aidd's default | Options |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `api-framework` | Which framework serves the API? | The framework the service already uses. For a new service, the ecosystem's common framework that serves the OpenAPI contract. | FastAPI, Hono, NestJS, ASP.NET Core minimal APIs, Spring Boot, axum, Go net/http |
| `validation-library` | Which library validates input against the contract at the boundary? | A schema library that the contract and the types come from, so one definition checks the input and documents it. | Pydantic, Zod, Valibot, JSON Schema with a validator, the framework's own validation |
| `api-test` | Which runner sends the API test requests to the running service and checks each response? | Hurl: plain-text request files in the repository, run by a command whose exit code fails the run. Bruno where the team wants a desktop app, with its collections kept as files in the repository too. | Hurl, Bruno, Postman, the framework's own HTTP test client |
| `load-test` | Which runner drives the load test, with the SLO as its pass or fail thresholds? | k6, with the SLO as thresholds in the script, so a missed threshold fails the run. Locust for a team that writes Python, and Gatling for a JVM team. | k6, Locust, Gatling |
